comment_data.body:
I think the original intention was to keep the activation platform agnostic but this is a pure Unix path. Gdb works on Windows, so I wouldn't use a simple path construction to rule out the chance of anyone using it.

The corresponding Windows path is `f"{virtualenv}\\Lib\\site-packages"`.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -52,11 +52,8 @@ def make_command_file(path_to_debug_info, prefix_code='',
                 import os
                 virtualenv = os.getenv('VIRTUAL_ENV')
                 if virtualenv:
-                    path_to_activate_this_py = os.path.join(virtualenv, 'bin', 'activate_this.py')
-                    print("gdb command file: Activating virtualenv: %s; path_to_activate_this_py: %s" % (
-                        virtualenv, path_to_activate_this_py))
-                    with open(path_to_activate_this_py) as f:
-                        exec(f.read(), dict(__file__=path_to_activate_this_py))
+                    sys.path.insert(0, f"{virtualenv}/lib/python{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}/site-packages")

comment_data.body:
I've updated this in a way that I think should work on Windows too without any real knowledge of how the paths are structured - essentially using the configuration in the interpreter using cygdb to work out what to add for the virtual environment.

This at least gets me through the activate virtual environment stage of cygdb successfully

milestone.description:
Main features:
- Pattern matching
- Generics / subscripted container types
- `@cython.collection_type()`
- `restrict`
- more vectorcalls
- more thread safety
- smaller modules, more shared code
- remove Py3.8 support, keep Py3.9+
